question: How do I get a new water connection for my house?
expected_data_source: NONE -- no KnowledgeRecord exists for this service in any tier
expected_information: Application process, required documents, security/scrutiny fee, designated officer, process time limit
notes: The current knowledge base contains complaint/grievance-type services only (report a problem), not service-request/application-type services (apply for something new). IMPORTANT self-audit finding: the source PDFs actually used for Mohali and Patiala DO list 'New Water Connection' as a service (7 days in Mohali, 9 days in Patiala, per their Services Standards tables) -- this data exists in the already-verified source documents but was never transcribed into a KnowledgeRecord, because Phase 1 scoped extraction to complaint-type sub-services only. This is a real, fixable gap, not a case of the source lacking the data.

question: How do I apply for a new electricity connection?
expected_data_source: NONE -- no source in sources/inventory.json covers electricity at all
expected_information: Which DISCOM/electricity board to contact, application process, documents, fee, timeline
notes: Unlike CSQ_NEWSVC_01/02, this is not a 'we have the source but didn't transcribe it' gap -- none of the 4 sources in inventory.json (3 municipal citizen charters + 1 synthetic placeholder) are electricity-board documents. Electricity connections/meters/billing in India are typically handled by a separate state DISCOM (e.g. PSPCL for Punjab, TPCODL for Odisha's Bhubaneswar circle), not the municipal corporations these charters cover. A future source-research pass targeting DISCOM citizen charters would be required.

question: Does the current knowledge base contain ANY 'new service application' record (as opposed to a complaint/repair record)?
expected_data_source: Verified by full-text scan of all 126 KnowledgeRecords
expected_information: Whether any record's problem_type describes a new-application service rather than a fault/complaint
notes: Confirmed by direct inspection of all 14 VERIFIED and all 112 SYNTHETIC records' service_name/sub_service/problem_type fields: every single one of the 126 records is a complaint/fault/repair-type service. Zero are new-connection, new-installation, or new-application service requests. This is a structural characteristic of the current data set, not a bug -- it matches the original Phase 1 scoping decision, but is worth calling out explicitly since the user-facing app is named 'JanSarthi' (broad civic assistant), not just a complaint tracker.

question: Are working hours available for Mohali's complaint centre?
expected_data_source: PB_MOHALI_WASTE_SOLID_WASTE, PB_MOHALI_WATER_SUPPLY_SEWERAGE (hours stated); PB_MOHALI_ROADS_CIVIL_WORKS, PB_MOHALI_STREETLIGHTS_REPAIR (hours not restated)
expected_information: Complaint Centre: 9:00 AM-4:00 PM; toll-free line: 9:30 AM-4:00 PM, working days only
notes: Self-audit finding: working hours are the SAME for all 4 Mohali services (same single complaint centre/toll-free system) but were only explicitly restated in 2 of the 4 Mohali KnowledgeRecords' procedure text. A retrieval system querying PB_MOHALI_ROADS_CIVIL_WORKS or PB_MOHALI_STREETLIGHTS_REPAIR alone would not surface the hours, even though they apply equally. Not a factual error, but an inconsistent-completeness issue worth normalizing later.

question: What is the fee for reporting uncollected garbage in Odisha?
expected_information: No fee (per the original source table's 'Fees / User charges' column, which states 'No fees' for this service)
notes: IMPORTANT self-audit finding: the source PDF's table explicitly states 'No fees' for this service (and for tube-well repair, WS pipeline repair, and street light replacement -- 4 of the 6 Odisha VERIFIED records), but this fact was NOT transcribed into any of those KnowledgeRecords' fields. The KB currently has no explicit 'fee' field at all -- fee information is only present where it was folded into free-text (as with the two road-cutting-related records, which do explicitly discuss fees). A retrieval system today would have no basis to answer 'is this free?' for solid waste/tube-well/WS-pipeline/street-light, even though the answer (yes, free) is sitting in the already-fetched, already-cited source document. Marked PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE rather than UNANSWERABLE because the source is verified and live, but the specific fact isn't in the record yet.

question: How do I report a pothole in Bhubaneswar, Odisha?
expected_information: A pothole/general-road-damage complaint process for Bhubaneswar or Odisha generally
notes: IMPORTANT self-audit finding: Odisha's two ROADS_POTHOLES-category VERIFIED records (OD_STATEWIDE_ROADS_ROAD_CUTTING_PERMISSION, OD_STATEWIDE_ROADS_ROAD_RESTORATION) are NOT general pothole complaints -- they cover getting permission to cut a road for utility work, and restoring a road after such authorized cutting. Neither covers a citizen reporting an ordinary pothole from wear and tear. Odisha's ROADS_POTHOLES category is therefore misleadingly named for this specific gap: it has zero coverage of the single most common civic complaint type (potholes) despite the category existing. Bhubaneswar (Odisha's capital and largest city) also has no SYNTHETIC record, since Odisha is entirely outside the 28-city synthetic list. Net result: total gap for this extremely common question in Odisha.
